question: Pipe A can fill an empty cistern alone in 26 hours and pipe B can fill the same cistern alone in 36 hours. The time taken by them to fill half of the cistern by operating together will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency = (1/26 + 1/36) cistern per hour.

Time to fill full cistern = (26 × 36) / (26 + 36) = 936 / 62 = 468 / 31 hours.

Time to fill **half cistern** = (1/2) × (468 / 31) = 234 / 31 hours.

234 / 31 = 7(17/31) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7(17)/(31) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ **Total Work (LCM of 26 and 36)** = 468 units

⇒ **Efficiency of A** = 468 ÷ 26 = 18 units/hour

⇒ **Efficiency of B** = 468 ÷ 36 = 13 units/hour

⇒ **Combined Efficiency (A + B)** = 18 + 13 = 31 units/hour

⇒ **Half of Total Work** = 468 ÷ 2 = 234 units

⇒ **Time taken** = 234 ÷ 31 = 7(17/31) hours

**∴ The correct answer is 7(17)/(31) hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B in 'y' hours, together they fill in (xy)/(x+y) hours.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes have **positive efficiency** while outlet (leakage) pipes have **negative efficiency**.

Partial Work Rule

Time taken to complete 'n' fraction of work = n × Total time required for full work.</p
